description:
PF5 on a user identifier no USRSEC row carries - THE MISSING GUARD at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:188-192, which is this folder's UNGUARDED-DELETE ANCHOR and the one case where the read-for-update fails and the delete FIRES ANYWAY. The four lines are the whole of it: IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON, MOVE USRIDINI OF COUSR3AI TO SEC-USR-ID, PERFORM READ-USER-SEC-FILE, PERFORM DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE, END-IF. The guard is evaluated EXACTLY ONCE, before the read, and there is NO second IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON between the two PERFORMs - so when the read raises WS-ERR-FLG on a NOTFND at :288 the delete at :191 runs regardless, with no record held. That is the precise reading of 'the read fails and no delete occurs': the delete CALL occurs, the record REMOVAL does not. Both halves are asserted here - the DISPLAY and the message the attempt produces, and the ten rows that prove nothing was removed. THE STRUCTURE IS MODELLED AS WRITTEN, NOT AS INTENDED: adding the guard the code obviously wants, or short-circuiting after the failed read, would be a redesign - it would leave exactly the TWO lines and NO DISPLAY that case07 pins for this same read outcome, where the source emits THREE of which that DISPLAY is the first - and it is exactly the instinct this case exists to catch. EIBCALEN is 194, so :90 takes its ELSE arm and :94 copies the commarea in; CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is already 1 (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), so :95 falls through to the ELSE at :106 and the unconditional first-entry send at :105 is never reached. :107 performs RECEIVE-USRDEL-SCREEN, whose EXEC CICS RECEIVE at :232-238 captures RESP and RESP2 into WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD and then NEVER EVALUATES THEM - this program has no receive-failure branch and none is invented. :108-130 evaluates EIBAID over six ordered arms - DFHENTER, DFHPF3, DFHPF4, DFHPF5, DFHPF12, WHEN OTHER - and the FOURTH matches, so :122 performs DELETE-USER-INFO; the order is itself an assertion, because a translation that matched DFHENTER first would run PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, whose two SEPARATE guards at :156-169 do stop after a failed read. Inside DELETE-USER-INFO the test at :177 is false, USRIDINI carrying NOSUCH02, so the WHEN OTHER arm at :183-185 moves -1 into USRIDINL and reaches a CONTINUE that does nothing; no error is raised, so the :188 guard is entered. NOSUCH02 IS A DELIBERATELY ABSENT KEY: a not-found arm needs a key the file genuinely does not hold, and this one is eight bytes so it needs no padding and cannot collide with ADMIN00n or USER000n. It is distinct from the NOSUCH01 that case07 uses for the ENTER path, so the two cases stay individually traceable. NOTHING IS FORCED, and that is deliberate: the absence of the row is what makes READ-USER-SEC-FILE's EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 report FileStatus.Outcome NOT_FOUND, and the empty hold is what makes the keyless DELETE report INVREQ, so the repository performs a real lookup and a real refusal rather than being told what to answer. That is strictly stronger than forcing, because it exercises the key comparison and the hold precondition as well as the two branches; forcedOutcomes is reserved for arms no seeded data can reach, such as the NOTOPEN case11 forces. THE READ'S NOTFND ARM at :287-292 runs first: 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, 'User ID NOT found...' into WS-MESSAGE, -1 into USRIDINL, and PERFORM SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN - SEND 1 OF 2, and no DISPLAY on this arm. THE DELETE RUNS ANYWAY. EXEC CICS DELETE at :307-311 names DATASET, RESP and RESP2 and NO RIDFLD, so it removes the record the preceding READ ... UPDATE left the task HOLDING and never one located by key - which is why the repository contract is readForUpdate followed by deleteHeld rather than a single delete(id): only the two-step shape can express 'the read failed, and the delete was still attempted against nothing'. With nothing held the command can name no record, CICS answers INVREQ - RESP 16, common.FileStatus.INVREQ, with RESP2 0, common.FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE - and no repository delete is issued at all, so the observable trace is a read-for-update and NO DELETE OF ANY KIND. INVREQ is NOT the not-found condition: EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :313-336 enumerates only NORMAL and NOTFND, so 16 reaches WHEN OTHER exactly as any other unenumerated response would, and an arm added for it would invent behaviour. THE WHEN OTHER ARM at :329-335 is asserted IN SOURCE ORDER: the DISPLAY at :330 is LIVE - the equivalent statement in COUSR01C is commented out, this one is not - and is emitted BEFORE the screen, which is why it is the first entry of expectedMessages; then 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG at :331, already 'Y' from the read; then the message at :332-333; then MOVE -1 TO FNAMEL at :334; then the send at :335, SEND 2 OF 2. THE PRESERVED DEFECT: :332-333 moves 'Unable to Update User...' into WS-MESSAGE. The word is 'Update', capitalised, inside a paragraph named DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE, on the failure path of an EXEC CICS DELETE - a copy/paste slip inherited from COUSR02C's rewrite path. It is reproduced BYTE FOR BYTE and is deliberately NOT corrected to 'Delete': capital U in Unable, capital U in Update, capital U in User, exactly three dots, no space before them. Writing what the code obviously MEANT would be an unrequested behaviour change, would breach the like-for-like migration mandate and would fail field-for-field diffing, so BOTH the unguarded delete and this wording are recorded here as KNOWN INHERITED BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED ON PURPOSE and are not errors in this fixture. THREE LINES ARE PINNED IN EMISSION ORDER AND THE ORDER IS ITSELF THE ASSERTION: the DISPLAY of :330, then the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE that :332-333 leaves, then the 78-byte ERRMSGO that MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :217 right-truncates it into. The three travel on their own channels at their own declared widths precisely so the two bytes the 80-to-78 move loses cannot go unnoticed; a move that truncated on the left would fail the 78-byte expectation while the 80-byte one still passed. The read's 'User ID NOT found...' is NOT among them because :332-333 OVERWRITES WS-MESSAGE before the second send, so it is no longer the message any channel holds when the task ends - it is pinned instead by the SEND COUNT OF TWO, the first of which exists only because the read's NOTFND arm sent. THE DISPLAY RENDERING, stated so a reviewer can audit it: WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD are PIC S9(09) COMP at :43-44, and a COBOL DISPLAY of a binary item converts it to display form, so each renders as nine zero-filled digits with no sign and no separator - 'RESP:' then 000000016 then 'REAS:' then 000000000, one line of exactly 28 characters on the variable-width DISPLAY_LINE channel, in the same shape case08 and case11 pin for their own WHEN OTHER arms and differing only in the RESP the condition carries. THE PRESERVED CURSOR QUIRK: :334 moves -1 into FNAMEL and not into USRIDINL, so the cursor lands on the FIRST NAME field even though the user id is what an operator would fix - and app/bms/COUSR03.bms:103 declares FNAME as ATTRB=(ASKIP,FSET,NORM), a field that cannot be typed into at all. The read's NOTFND arm did move it to USRIDINL at :291, and the delete's own NOTFND arm does so at :327, so this is a divergence rather than a shared convention: cursorField is FNAMEL and USRIDINL is not restored, because repairing an inherited cursor target would be an unrequested behaviour change. FNAMEL is symbolic-map metadata - an xxxL length item at app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY:61 - so it is reported through cursorField and is deliberately not modelled as a payload member; the payload is the eleven xxxI items COUSR03.CPY declares and nothing else, and COUSR03 has no password item at all. NOTHING IS BLANKED: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :349-356 runs only on the delete's NORMAL arm at :315 and on PF4 at :120, never here, and DELETE-USER-INFO has no equivalent of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY's :157-159 clear, so USRIDINO still reads NOSUCH02 and FNAMEO, LNAMEO and USRTYPEO still carry the LAWRENCE, THOMAS and U the terminal transmitted. Those three are USER0001's real values on purpose: all eleven named fields of app/bms/COUSR03.bms are FSET so the terminal returns every one of them, and a translation that copied :157-159 into this paragraph would blank a genuine user's name and be caught here. That is the material difference from case07, which reaches the SAME repository outcome on the read by the ENTER path and does blank all three. ERRMSGC IS DERIVED, NOT COPIED: neither the read's NOTFND arm nor the delete's WHEN OTHER arm writes the colour byte, so it keeps the default of DFHDFCOL and the field renders red from ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET), COLOR=RED at app/bms/COUSR03.bms:140-143, baked into the physical map rather than moved by the program. This is NOT case11's DFHNEUTR: there the read's NORMAL arm had already written it at :285, and here the read never took that arm. DFHGREEN would be the delete-success arm at :317 and is not asserted either. Re-entry carrying an error is the state in which an error highlight applies, and it is applied inline because COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY; the mnemonic comes from common.BmsAttributes, which reproduces the absent IBM-supplied DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR from IBM CICS documentation, as common.CicsAid does for DFHAID and its DFHPF5 (risk R-D). Two sends are performed and the count is behaviour: SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN at :213-225 repaints all six header items through POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :243-262 on both, and only the last leaves the five variable items and the colour byte the terminal is left showing. :134-137 then returns with TRANSID(WS-TRANID), so the conversation stays on CU03. THE RETURN CODE IS 0 as a positive assertion rather than a default: COUSR03C contains zero CALL 'CEE3ABD' sites and never moves a severity into RETURN-CODE, so neither the failed lookup nor the refused delete abends however severe either looks. USRSEC IS UNCHANGED, which is what 'no delete occurs' means precisely: expectedWrites is empty - a positive assertion that nothing was written, not an absence of interest - and ALL TEN rows are pinned at zero-based indices 0 through 9, each by its six CSUSR01Y names and as its whole eighty-byte image. SEC-USR-FILLER is pinned BY NAME as twenty-three spaces, because 8 + 20 + 20 + 8 + 1 = 57 and only that filler carries the record to the 80 that RECORDSIZE(80,80) at app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:64-66 and LRECL=80 at :48 declare; a codec that omitted it would fail on the total width alone. The literal PASSWORD in SEC-USR-PWD is legacy sample data carried byte for byte because app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:21 places it inside the eighty bytes - plaintext credentials are an inherited property of the legacy design rather than a choice made here, this screen has no password field among its eleven xxxI items and never paints or reads that span, and no hashing, encoding or token is introduced. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key USRSEC and never by a dataset name. The communication area, the AID and the screen values travel in the payload alone: no server-side session state, in keeping with the pseudo-conversational contract. NO USER RULES GOVERN THIS FILE: review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided.', which is the whole document; no rule has been invented and the absence is not treated as permission to lower the bar - the enterprise practices of the plan govern instead. PROVENANCE: every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:188-192, the read's NOTFND arm at :287-292 and the delete's WHEN OTHER arm at :329-335, together with :106-137, :174-192, :213-225, :232-238, :243-262, :302-336 and :349-356, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 for the six spans, app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY for the eleven xxxI items and the FNAMEL length item at :61, app/bms/COUSR03.bms:103 and :140-143 for the field attributes, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 with app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:50-58 for the 194-byte area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 for the two forty-character titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header clock, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy for the shared message structures, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-99 whose DELETE(YES) at :94 authorises this path, and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, with the clock pinned to the version footer at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:358 exactly as case01 pins it. It is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL: running it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler's indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository - which is the documented eight-blocker deviation escalated as risk R-A. It changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else: the twenty cases, the field-by-field diffing and the zero-diff gate all stand.

THE OPERATION ORDER, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every USRSEC operation this case must issue, in order, and it is an assertion a byte fingerprint structurally cannot make: the EXEC CICS DELETE at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:307-311 names no RIDFLD, so it removes the record the task is HOLDING and is only ever correct after the EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 took that hold on the same record. An empty list is equally an assertion - it says this path never reached the file at all.

THE FIRST SEND CARRIES THE WHOLE MAP AREA. EXEC CICS SEND MAP('COUSR3A') MAPSET('COUSR03') FROM(COUSR3AO) ERASE CURSOR at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:219-225 transmits the entire symbolic-map area, not the items the sending paragraph happened to touch, so all eleven xxxO items are on the wire at the first send exactly as they are at the last - and :217 moves WS-MESSAGE to ERRMSGO on every one of them. Because COUSR3AO REDEFINES COUSR3AI in app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY, the four writable items still hold precisely what the terminal sent: DELETE-USER-INFO at :174-192 - unlike PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :156-159 and :164-166 - never moves SPACES over FNAMEI, LNAMEI and USRTYPEI and never re-populates them from the record, so USRIDINO, FNAMEO, LNAMEO and USRTYPEO echo this case's received mapFields padded to their declared PIC X widths. ERRMSGO and ERRMSGC on the first send are the DFHRESP(NOTFND) arm at :287-292, which moves no colour at all, so ERRMSGC still holds the map's default DFHDFCOL. Pinning all eleven on sends[0] is what makes the two sends distinguishable rather than merely countable: the second differs from the first only in ERRMSGO, in ERRMSGC, and in whatever INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :349-355 cleared.
